text: Every push to main runs its gate to the end, and the dashboard reads receipts only from a gate that ran. The morning the repository went public, #37, #35, #36 and #38 merged within minutes. Each push to main cancelled the run before it, and GitHub also drops a waiting run when a newer one joins its concurrency group. #38 changed only docs, so its gate was skipped. That left main's code with no gate run on main. The public dashboard took #38's run, which uploaded no receipts, so it showed 1 project of 13 and said the gate passed. Now each push to main has a concurrency group of its own, and only a newer push to a pull request cancels its run. The dashboard takes receipts from the newest run whose gate ran, and says a gate was skipped when only docs changed. A re-run of #36's merge gated main's code.
